backup.introBody: Nothing leaves this phone unless you say so. That makes it private, and it makes backing up your job. Here are five ways it happens, from the one that needs nothing to the one that needs you.
backup.holding: Right now: {{photos}} bill photos, {{size}} of them.
backup.googleBody: Android quietly copies this app's data to a private area of your Google Drive — your transactions, budgets and settings. Set up a new phone with the same Google account and it comes back when you reinstall.
backup.googleCaveat: Android caps this at 25 MB per app and backs up nothing at all once you pass it, so bill photos are deliberately kept out — otherwise a few hundred receipts would take your whole backup down with them. It runs about once a day on Wi-Fi, and it disappears if you uninstall the app. Safety net, not the plan.
backup.autoBody: A copy of your data saved inside the app, on a schedule. The last {{keep}} are kept, so you can go back to before a bad import or a wrong delete. Photos aren't in these — they travel in the ZIP copies below.
backup.folderBody: Pick a folder once — Downloads, an SD card — and every automatic backup also lands there as a ZIP with your bill photos inside. Useful when you want a copy you can hand straight to a computer. The last {{keep}} are kept.
backup.folderNone: No folder chosen. Backups stay inside the app only.
backup.folderChosen: Folder set. A copy has been saved there now.
backup.folderForgotten: Stopped. Files already saved there are untouched.
backup.manualBody: One ZIP with everything — data and every bill photo. This is the one to send yourself before changing phones.
backup.csvCaveat: JSON is readable in any text editor. The .db file is the database itself. CSV is for a spreadsheet and cannot restore budgets, rules or categories.
backup.driveBody: Connect your Google account and every automatic backup also goes to a folder called “{{folder}}” in your own Drive — a full ZIP with your bill photos inside, and no 25 MB limit. This is the only copy that survives both losing the phone and uninstalling the app. The last {{keep}} are kept.
backup.driveScope: The app can only see files it creates itself. It cannot read anything else in your Drive.
backup.driveOn: On — saving to “{{folder}}” in your Drive
backup.driveStopBody: Backups already in your Drive stay there — this app will not delete them. It just stops adding new ones.
backup.driveRevokeHint: To also take back the app's access, open your Google Account, then Security, then your connections to third-party apps.
backup.driveOldBuild: This app was installed before Drive backup was added. Install the newer version and it will appear here.
backup.driveConnected: Connected. A full copy with your photos is now in your Drive.
backup.driveConnectedNoCopy: Connected. The first copy didn't upload — it will try again with the next backup.
backup.driveDisconnected: Stopped. Copies already in your Drive were left alone.
backup.driveReason.signIn: Google needs you to sign in again
backup.driveReason.full: your Google account is out of storage
backup.driveReason.permission: the app no longer has permission
backup.tookButDrive: Backed up on this phone, but the copy to Drive didn't go through. It will try again with the next backup.
backup.driveNotRegistered: Google closed the sign-in without connecting. Almost always this means this build's app signature isn't registered in your Google Cloud project yet.
backup.driveNoResult: The Google screen closed without giving an answer. Try once more; if it keeps happening, the sign-in is being interrupted before it finishes.
backup.driveApiError: Signed in, but Google Drive rejected the request: {{reason}}. If this mentions the Drive API, it needs enabling on your Cloud project.
backup.driveFixBody: Google matches an app by its package name and the fingerprint of the key that signed it. Add these two, exactly as shown, as an Android client in the Google Cloud Console at console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients. This fingerprint is read from the app running right now, so it is the correct one whichever keystore built it.
backup.driveFingerprintShared: Sent. Paste them into the Android OAuth client.

backup.driveClosed: The Google screen closed without connecting. Two usual causes: your Google account isn't on the project's Test users list, or this build's app signature isn't registered. The details below cover the second.

notify.troubleBody: Many phones — Xiaomi, Redmi, Oppo, Vivo, Realme, Samsung — stop background reminders to save battery. The app cannot override that, but one setting fixes it:
notify.troublePath: Settings → Apps → Expense Tracker → Battery → Unrestricted (or “No restrictions”, “Allow background activity”)
notify.troubleTiming: Reminders can also arrive a few minutes late. Android decides when to deliver them, and an expense reminder is not allowed to override battery saving.
notify.privacyBody: Every reminder is worked out on this phone from your own entries. Nothing is sent to a server, and there is nothing to switch on anywhere else.
